question: Does explicitly aligning ordered source/target information across query and scene representations improve unseen-pair role transfer beyond a matched unordered-identity objective?
model: Same two-tower listener. Auxiliary arms add two shared 10-class linear heads; both heads are applied to the normalized query and correct-scene embeddings. Auxiliary heads are unused at evaluation.
unordered_control_targets: lower identity index of two participants
higher identity index of two participants
loss: Original four-choice cross entropy plus 0.5 times the mean of four auxiliary cross entropies (two heads x query/scene).
evaluation: All 45 pairs, 512 renderings per pair, two fixed scene seeds as in generator_gate_v1. Primary development comparison is paired mean unseen binary role accuracy; also report seen four-choice, unseen event, and weak-pair incidence.
advance_only_if: Ordered-role arm improves over both balanced baseline and unordered-identity control on all three graph means, with familiar four-choice at least 0.99 and no material event loss. This is a development gate, not a significance test.
no_test_leakage: No unobserved pair contributes to training or auxiliary targets. No evaluation outcome changes objective weight or stopping step during this block.
interpretation_limits: A gain would demonstrate a useful training signal here, not that baseline representations lacked roles
Source motion remains a perceptual cue
The graphs have been inspected previously, so any advancing claim needs untouched graph confirmation
